name: Analytical Marxism
summary: Analytical Marxism is an academic school, active from the late 1970s, that restates Marx's questions about class, exploitation and history using analytical philosophy, rational-choice theory and neoclassical economics. It keeps an egalitarian, socialist ethical aim but drops the labour theory of value, dialectics and much of the classical theory of revolution. Its members favour democratic and often market-based forms of socialism with far more equal ownership of productive assets.
scope: The September Group strand: G. A. Cohen (Karl Marx's Theory of History, Why Not Socialism?), John Roemer (A General Theory of Exploitation and Class, A Future for Socialism), Jon Elster (Making Sense of Marx), Erik Olin Wright (Classes, Real Utopias), Adam Przeworski and Philippe Van Parijs. Many statements in the bank are far from this school's concerns and are answered by inference at low confidence.

keyFigures.name: G. A. Cohen
keyFigures.role: Founder of the approach with Karl Marx's Theory of History (1978) and later egalitarian political philosophy.

keyFigures.name: John Roemer
keyFigures.role: Developed the general theory of exploitation and class and models of market socialism.

keyFigures.name: Jon Elster
keyFigures.role: Applied rational choice and methodological individualism in Making Sense of Marx.

sources.author: Harry Brighouse, Crooked Timber
sources.usedFor: Cohen's argument that socialism rests on equality of opportunity and community, via the camping trip; used as a secondary summary of that work.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred from the egalitarian commitment to equalising access to resources regardless of endowments.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Never discussed specifically; inferred from concern about unequal bargaining positions of propertyless workers, though analytical Marxists favour changing asset distribution over wage tinkering.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Roemer and others accept markets for allocation but see market outcomes as resting on unjust asset distribution; they do not claim markets beat governments in general.

public-ownership.rationale: Socialism for this school means redistributing or socialising productive assets, though often via market-socialist mechanisms such as equal coupon shares rather than state industry.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The school's egalitarianism targets unequal ownership of productive assets, which implies support for taxing the rich, but its proposals centre on redistributing ownership (Roemer's coupon socialism) rather than on tax rates.

unions-good.rationale: Wright and Przeworski treat organised labour as central to the class compromise and to workers' power, though unions are not a focus of the theory.

property-fundamental.rationale: Roemer calls capitalism unjust because of unequal ownership of the means of production, so no property right is treated as beyond override.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian aims; the school prefers changing ownership structure to regulation, so the answer is mild.

cut-welfare.rationale: Egalitarian redistribution is the heart of the programme; welfare cuts run against it, and dependency arguments are not part of the school.

worker-ownership.rationale: Roemer's market socialism and Wright's real utopias include worker-owned firms, though not all analytical Marxists make it the sole model.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the liberal-egalitarian civil-liberties stance of the school, which rejects trading rights for security.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the academic left-liberal outlook of the school and its rejection of paternalism.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed, and left-liberal academics are split on legal restriction.

strong-leader.rationale: Analytical Marxists favour democratic accountability and reject authoritarian shortcuts as a route to socialism.

state-harmful.rationale: The school argues for a democratic egalitarian state that redistributes property; it does not regard the state as inherently harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no shared position.

empower-police-military.rationale: Roemer notes police power protects unequal property, so more authority is unwelcome, but the topic is not developed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed and adherents plausibly split between exploitation worries and liberal tolerance.

decide-locally.rationale: Neither centralism nor localism is a principle of the school; Wright favours participatory forms but also national redistribution.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian emphasis on social causes of disadvantage.

traditional-family.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the secular egalitarian outlook, which treats family structure as no foundation of justice.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the left-liberal outlook of adherents.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the left-liberal outlook of adherents.

more-religion-public.rationale: Marx's secular view of religion carries over, and analytical Marxists are secular academics, but the matter is not discussed.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian view that unjustly inherited advantages should be corrected, though race is peripheral to the school's class focus.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; the school's stress on empirical rigour makes a firm view unlikely.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Not addressed; class and distribution, not national culture, organise the school, and its outlook is cosmopolitan.

gradual-change.rationale: Przeworski defends democratic reformism while Cohen and Wright also talk about transformation, so adherents mix reform and deeper change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; Van Parijs argues for open or very liberal borders in the same egalitarian tradition, but not all members do.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not addressed; some cosmopolitan sympathy but no shared position.

free-trade.rationale: Roemer analyses unequal exchange between countries as exploitation, so claims that free trade benefits everyone are doubted.

nation-first.rationale: Egalitarian universalism rejects putting national interest ahead of global cooperation, though the school did not address it directly.

open-borders.rationale: Van Parijs defends open borders on egalitarian grounds, but it is not a school-wide view.

limit-growth.rationale: Cohen's productive-forces thesis stresses growth historically, but later egalitarians accept limits; not a shared view.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the school's science-respecting, left-egalitarian outlook.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Cohen holds that productive forces develop and enable emancipation, but the school does not believe technology alone solves social problems.

revolution-justified.rationale: Many analytical Marxists judged the classical theory of revolution compromised and favour democratic routes, but do not rule it out.

experts-over-public.rationale: Democratic self-determination is valued, though the school prizes rigorous expertise; not directly discussed.

central-planning.rationale: Roemer and others turned to market socialism, accepting that central planning had failed on efficiency and incentives.

socialized-markets.rationale: Roemer's market socialism and Wright's real utopias explicitly support markets with socially owned or equally distributed capital.

land-value-tax.rationale: Left-libertarian egalitarians like Van Parijs and Steiner discuss natural-resource taxes, but the school has no shared position.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Roemer lists inheritance among the sources of unjust unequal endowments, which supports heavy taxation of large inheritances.

basic-income.rationale: Van Parijs, a September Group member, is the leading basic-income theorist, and others sympathise; it is not universal in the school.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no shared position.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Roemer's models use public banks that direct capital within a market, but the school disagrees on state steering.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The school wants productive assets equalised or socially held, not distributed among small private owners, though equal endowments appear in Roemer's models.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Market socialists accept markets and wages in a transitional or lasting socialism, and the school rejects utopian blueprints of abolition.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Nothing in the school supports abolishing central banks; its market socialism uses public banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; Przeworski's analysis of class compromise is not state-corporatist, but the topic is peripheral.

one-party-rule.rationale: The school accepts liberal democracy and rejects vanguard rule, and its members criticise Soviet-type systems.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian and democratic principles.

democracy-best.rationale: Przeworski defends democracy as the arena of socialist politics, though the school allows that democracy may fail egalitarian aims.

direct-votes.rationale: Wright's empowered participatory governance favours direct participation but not plebiscites on laws.

workers-councils.rationale: Not a central claim; the school favours democratic state institutions with workplace democracy alongside.

natural-rulers.rationale: The school's egalitarianism rejects natural rulers as unjustified advantage.

political-violence-never.rationale: Not addressed; adherents doubt classical revolution but have no absolute pacifist position.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal-egalitarian outlook which rejects this militarist claim.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the secular liberal-egalitarian outlook.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from secular rationalism and Marx's critique of religion.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Roemer notes policing protects unequal property, and the school rejects market anarchism of the right-libertarian sort.

military-superiority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from cosmopolitan egalitarianism.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from universalist egalitarian principles.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Cohen reads history through productive forces, with class struggle derived, and Elster rejects any general theory of history, so the school gives class conflict less primacy than orthodox Marxism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Cohen's socialist equality of opportunity extends to correcting differences from luck and circumstance, though they do not demand strict equal outcomes.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Roemer discusses unequal exchange between countries, but reparations are not a stated position.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from universalist outlook.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Cohen's camping-trip argument holds that community and mutual care, not self-interest, are the proper ideals.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not addressed; liberal-egalitarian emphasis on rights, though Cohen values community.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Cohen's thesis treats productive development as the basis for human liberation, so adherents reject this claim.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Cohen's development thesis favours productive growth, but disruption of institutions is not a school goal.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic commitments.

restore-past-order.rationale: The school is progressive and reconstructs Marx's account of historical development toward socialism.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The school rejects dialectical dogma for empirical testing and logical rigour, so judging claims by evidence fits its method.

direct-action.rationale: Przeworski's work emphasises electoral politics, and Wright favours institutional strategies, so direct action is not the school's route.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Cohen's thesis of productive progress treats a return to foraging as the opposite of emancipation.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marx envisaged overcoming the division of labour, but analytical Marxists accept specialisation and doubt this utopian aim.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Cohen's community principle and Marx's higher-stage maxim point to need-based distribution, though Roemer questions its feasibility soon.

production-for-use.rationale: Market socialists accept production for profit-seeking firms under social ownership of capital, so production for use is not a school demand.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Roemer argues that all commodities are exploited under capitalism so exploitation of labour does not explain profits, and Cohen drops the labour theory.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The school treats democratic politics as the route to socialism and rejects dictatorial rule as a defensible institution.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed; Roemer's equal-endowment models favour individual or cooperative holdings, not compulsory collectives.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed; the school is sceptical of deterministic claims about capitalism's inevitable outcomes.

taxation-theft.rationale: Cohen's critique of Nozick treats taxation as compatible with justice, since self-ownership does not give unlimited property rights.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; left-liberal sympathy but no stated position.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Not addressed; adherents hold methodological individualism, but this is about explanation, not rights.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal-egalitarian values, with some adherents open to civic service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; adherents give priority to democratic voice and egalitarian participation.

state-as-business.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian and democratic values.

positive-liberty.rationale: Cohen argues proletarians suffer unfreedom from lacking property, so freedom needs material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; the school holds that economic power outweighs both.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian outlook and scientific standards.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal-democratic assumptions.

total-state.rationale: The school accepts liberal-democratic institutions and criticises the Soviet model.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from universalist egalitarian outlook.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from cosmopolitan egalitarianism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic egalitarian principles.

bound-labor.rationale: Roemer treats feudal bondage as a form of exploitation and as unjust.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The school rejects dialectical and relativist traditions in favour of logical rigour and empirical testability.

universal-morality.rationale: Cohen defends egalitarian principles as moral truths and the school treats ethical argument as rational and general.

single-common-good.rationale: Not addressed; analytical Marxists accept interest conflict between classes but also advocate moral principles.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Roemer links socialist revolution to industrial democracy and Wright supports democratic firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from preference for equal public provision.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed; Przeworski's social democracy accepts activist fiscal policy.

economic-freedom.rationale: Cohen argues that capitalist freedom is a freedom of owners and that workers lack real freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from preference for institutions and rational justification.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal-cosmopolitan orientation.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Inferred from the school's commitment to analytic rigour and empirical testing in social theory; the statement's claim that reason is the only guide to knowledge and action is a broader philosophical thesis the sources do not take up.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; egalitarian universalism, with Van Parijs debating the tension.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; Van Parijs argues for unconditional income against work requirements.

class-collaboration.rationale: Roemer and Wright treat class conflict over assets as real, though Przeworski's analysis allows class compromise.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from scholarly culture.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from internationalist egalitarianism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian outlook.

ban-interest.rationale: Roemer's credit-market capitalism models treat lending as exploitation-neutral, so banning interest is not a goal.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not addressed; strongly against by egalitarian principles.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Elster analyses three models of the capitalist state and finds the instrumental view only one option, so adherents reject a simple version.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from left-egalitarian orientation.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal-egalitarian outlook.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not addressed; conspiracy theory incompatible with the school's rigour.

proportional-representation.rationale: Przeworski studies democratic institutions and class representation, but no stated position on electoral systems.

national-mission.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from universalist outlook.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian outlook, though Wright's class focus predominates.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian and liberal principles.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal-democratic values.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Roemer and Cohen reject the minimal state, with Cohen's critique of Nozick defending redistribution.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not addressed; strongly against by egalitarian values.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Cohen's egalitarianism rests on the equal moral standing of persons.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not addressed; analytical Marxists discuss socialism in market-socialist terms without this dogma.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal secular values.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from secular outlook.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from secular outlook.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not addressed; adherents reject Soviet-type doctrine.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Not directly addressed, but the school assumes democratic legitimacy as in Przeworski's democratic socialism.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from rejection of mercantilism by economically trained adherents.

population-transfer.rationale: Not addressed; strongly against by egalitarian principles.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Cohen's critique of Nozick specifically rejects this libertarian principle as grounding property rights.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Cohen treats cooperation and community as the ideal over competition.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Roemer distinguishes domination from exploitation, and Cohen's freedom argument has similar structure, but republicanism is not a school label.

vanguard-party.rationale: The school replaced Leninist theory with rational-choice analysis of class action, and rejects the vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Cohen's socialist principles and Roemer's egalitarianism give priority to the disadvantaged.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from pro-labour egalitarianism.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Roemer attributes poverty to unequal assets, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian outlook.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal-democratic values.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; economically trained adherents are cautious about price controls.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic commitments.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic commitments.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian cosmopolitanism.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Marx's Commune model includes this, but analytical Marxists do not take it up.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from rejection of vanguard organisation.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic commitments.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic values.

recall-officials.rationale: Marx's Commune model includes recall, but the school does not discuss it.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; market-oriented egalitarians would not ban renting.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not addressed; no support in the school.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from modernist, progressive outlook.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from left-liberal values.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from left-liberal values.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal values.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from cosmopolitan egalitarianism.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian multicultural liberalism.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal-intellectual outlook.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Roemer discusses unequal exchange between countries, but debt is not addressed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Roemer's view of political forms resting on property relations suggests it, though not about independence.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic commitments.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Roemer treats unequal exchange between countries as exploitation, so egalitarians infer duties to poor countries.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed; economically informed leftists typically oppose strict independence.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from cosmopolitan values.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Roemer holds that property rights lack independent moral authority and Cohen argues property must meet egalitarian tests.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed as such; analytical Marxists judge the USSR a failed socialism but diverge on labels.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic values.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Roemer's egalitarianism supports progressive taxation, which a flat tax opposes.

character-from-environment.rationale: Roemer's circumstance-versus-effort egalitarianism treats advantages as largely social, though not a stated theory of character.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic egalitarian values.

leader-cult.rationale: Not addressed; adherents reject Soviet-style cults.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Not addressed; adherents reject Maoist doctrine.

land-redistribution.rationale: Roemer's model treats unequal land ownership as the basis of feudal exploitation and favours more equal endowments.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Cohen defended the primacy of productive forces in explaining history, though Elster and others dispute a general theory.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian outlook.

moral-incentives.rationale: Cohen values community and Roemer explored efficiency, so adherents split on whether moral incentives can replace material ones.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Not addressed; focoism is foreign to the school.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Roemer's inequality theory treats unearned inherited advantage as unjust.

public-money-creation.rationale: Roemer's models include public banks, but money creation is not addressed.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Przeworski sees capitalism as adaptable via social democracy, while others expect decline, so adherents are split.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; Roemer analyses international exchange but market socialists accept trade.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Roemer's unequal exchange analysis supports some of it, but adherents hold nuanced class positions.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Cohen's egalitarian critique of libertarian freedom implies rejection.

minority-veto.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic values.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from analytic-ethics tradition.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Cohen rejects charity as a substitute for justice and community.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are politically engaged.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Marx's ideology theory suggests it, but the school is wary of functionalist claims.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not stressed by analytical Marxists; inferred as mixed.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Roemer analyses unequal exchange between countries, yet he applies it as a technical model, not world-systems theory.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from left-liberal values.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from historical scholarship.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Marx favoured recall under the Commune model, but the school is not committed.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian preference for pooled social insurance.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not addressed; Roemer's models of land tenure are descriptive.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Cohen is critical of materialist inequality, but there is no shared stance.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the school's critique of Soviet systems.

corporate-influence.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from concern about unequal power from property.

job-guarantee.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian aims.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not addressed; rejected on scholarly grounds.

informal-organisation.rationale: Not addressed; the school favours institutional strategies.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian redistribution across regions.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Marxian tradition keeps personal property while socialising productive property, which analytical Marxists share.

defeat-communism.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are socialists critical of Soviet communism, not anti-communist crusaders.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Market-socialist designs allow mixed provision, but no shared position.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marx's view of religion as a response to material alienation is largely shared by secular adherents, though not stressed.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Cohen's historical materialism sees capitalism as developing the productive forces that make socialism possible.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The school favours market-socialist designs at society scale, not small property-sharing communes.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Market socialism may be taken as a third path, but the school identifies as socialist and Marxist.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Rejected on scholarly grounds; not discussed in school texts.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The school treats democratic freedoms as essential and rejects the Soviet model.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Wright's empowered participatory governance and workplace democracy support the idea.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not addressed; Wright's class analysis is open to other oppressions but with no shared position.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The school identifies as left-wing Marxism and keeps class distribution at the centre.

alienated-labor.rationale: Roemer treats differential alienation as one possible reason for interest in exploitation, and Marx's concept is retained in a reduced form.

social-market-economy.rationale: Przeworski analyses social democracy, which fits this, but the school aims at more radical asset redistribution.

rich-first.rationale: The school favours equal starting endowments, not letting some grow rich first.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Roemer's market socialism uses publicly controlled banks, but interest-free credit is not addressed.

reification.rationale: The school discards Hegelian-style concepts like reification in favour of analytic reformulation, so adherents do not endorse the claim as stated.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from concern about unequal property power.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Roemer holds capitalism unjust because of unequal ownership of productive assets, and Cohen grounds socialism in equality, so concentrated wealth is a central target.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the liberal-egalitarian view that equal standing and freedom apply regardless of sexual orientation.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the school's analytical, liberal-egalitarian style, which favours state neutrality on belief.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the school's focus on distributive justice and democratic institutions rather than abolition of coercive agencies.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the majoritarian democratic socialism of members like Przeworski and Wright.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Cohen and Roemer ground socialism in equalising access through institutions and ownership rather than voluntary charity.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; the school has no settled view on term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from Wright's real utopias of participatory and empowered democracy, though delegable voting is not discussed.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the rationalist, welfare-minded approach that gives weight to long-run human outcomes.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the egalitarian commitments of Cohen and Wright.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the egalitarian commitments of Cohen and Wright.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian, universalist ethics of the school; it did not address local voting rights directly.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian aim of Why Not Socialism?, though members favour markets and might prefer other redistribution tools.

abolish-ip.rationale: Roemer's exploitation theory concerns unequal asset ownership; whether intellectual property counts is not stated, so members could differ.

uniformed-youth.rationale: An academic, individualist, rational-choice school is inferred to reject drilled national-service youth organisation.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from the school's egalitarian internationalism; nuclear policy is not discussed.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from internationalist and anti-imperialist socialist ethics; not addressed directly.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from the school's moral-philosophical egalitarianism; the sources do not mention genocide recognition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Roemer defines exploitation through income derived from unequal ownership of productive assets, and Cohen argues socialism should end rewards that rest on property rather than effort.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Rational-choice and analytical philosophy treat self-defence as typically justified; inferred, and not a topic of the school.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The school's methodological individualism and cosmopolitan egalitarianism are inferred to cut against national-origin myths.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; members' views on gender constructivism are not documented in the sources.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; no sourced position on feminist category debates.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: A secular, rationalist school is inferred to reject cults of martyrs and saints for the nation.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The school rejects dialectics and metaphysics in favour of analytic rigour and rational choice, so a spiritual-struggle view of politics is inferred to be rejected.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from the school's rationalist, class-based focus; cultural renewal as a prior task is not part of it.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; a secular school with no sourced view.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the school's egalitarianism and class analysis, which reject privileging economic control by an ethnic majority.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from internationalist egalitarianism; not addressed directly.

independent-unions.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred from the egalitarian aim of equalising bargaining power for propertyless workers.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from Wright's and Roemer's democratic socialism, which seeks real popular control over the economy.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to more equal and shared ownership of productive assets.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed; constitutional design lies outside the school's concerns.

municipal-property.rationale: Roemer's market socialism spreads ownership through equal individual shares, not municipal ownership; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no clear position can be inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian, anti-exploitation stance, which favours universal provision over wages tied to male earners.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; no clear position follows from the egalitarian principles.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed; egalitarians might back it but worry about unequal access to the results.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; no clear position follows from the school's principles.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-egalitarian side of the school, which values individual freedom.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from Cohen's work on self-ownership and the Kantian, individual-regarding basis of its egalitarianism.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The school keeps Marx's materialism but restates his ethics in secular philosophical terms; inferred.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not addressed; no clear position can be inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed; no clear position can be inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; no clear position can be inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from the class-based analysis of exploitation, which does not treat racial groups as the basis of political interests.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed; no clear position follows from the school's principles.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian ethical aim and the school's rejection of imperial aggression; not stated in the sources.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the school's universalist, individualist egalitarianism, which gives no weight to nation-forming language.

communal-electorates.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the school's liberal-egalitarian democratic commitments to equal citizenship in common institutions.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not addressed; academic rational-choice Marxists treat such conspiracy claims as poorly evidenced, which this is inferred from.

free-public-college.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from Roemer's and Cohen's aim of equalising access to assets such as education regardless of background.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not addressed; market-friendly members like Roemer would accept price instruments but others favour regulation or public investment, so inferred as split.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the school's egalitarian ethics, which Roemer and Van Parijs extend to fair shares across generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the school's analytical individualism, which resists generalising about group-typical values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the school's socialist, internationalist ethics and distrust of militarism.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the school's democratic and transparency-minded egalitarianism.

capital-controls.rationale: Not addressed; inferred market socialists accept some limits on capital but stress democratic ownership over border controls, so split.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: the school's democratic, reformist socialism assumes a legitimate democratic state with a monopoly of force.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and adherents have no shared view.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: Wright and Przeworski treat strong unions as part of egalitarian socialism, though the school focuses on asset ownership.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from the school's support for redistribution and income floors such as Van Parijs's basic income.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: binding borrowing limits would constrain egalitarian redistribution and public investment.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian ethics of Cohen and Roemer, which extend to unequal endowments between countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The sources describe it as dropping the classical theory of revolution in favour of democratic routes.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from Wright's Real Utopias and Roemer's market socialism, which test institutional designs without a single blueprint.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents with neoclassical tools may accept it while egalitarians doubt it.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred: the rationalist, individualist methodology and cosmopolitan egalitarianism treat nations as non-sacred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian aim of equalising access to resources regardless of endowments.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Their exploitation theory could cover regions but the sources do not apply it, and adherents are split.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Adherents are split: Cohen and Elster accept a stable human nature, while others follow Marx's historical view.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from the school's support for publicly provided goods and democratic institutions.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from its secular, rationalist analytic method; it treats religious claims as rival and unproven rather than as one shared truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred; the school favours market socialism and equal asset ownership, but nothing in the sources addresses farm price guarantees.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian and cosmopolitan ethics; the sources do not discuss nuclear deterrence.

workers-own-party.rationale: Przeworski and Wright examined socialist parties and class coalitions critically, and the school does not endorse a single independent workers' party.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from its egalitarian liberal ethic of equal freedom; the sources do not discuss the practice.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from its egalitarian ethic and concern with equal access to productive assets; inheritance law is not discussed directly.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A linguistic classification question the school never addressed.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from its preference for collective democratic choice and public regulation over private litigation.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from its democratic and egalitarian commitments, which disfavour formal roles for unelected traditional rulers.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents differ on how to trade liberty against collective ecological goals.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from its egalitarian, reformist ethic; sentencing is not discussed in the sources.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; Van Parijs wrote on linguistic justice but the sources opened here do not state a position.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from the school's egalitarian, pro-labour outlook; it did not address union security rules directly.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from its egalitarian emphasis on broad political participation; voter ID was not addressed.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from its liberal-egalitarian commitment to equal treatment and neutrality among beliefs.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Przeworski defends a minimal procedural view of democracy while Cohen and Wright want a more substantive, egalitarian one, so members are split.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the school's liberal-egalitarian ethics, which treat personal sexual choices as the individual's own.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from its liberal-egalitarian commitments to free communication and political participation.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from Roemer's and Van Parijs's support for market socialism and unconditional basic income, which resemble a single cash transfer.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from the school's commitment to the equal moral standing of persons; the members never debated suffrage as such.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Religion and gender were peripheral to the school, and Marxist views on the question vary.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from its egalitarian ethics and rejection of biological hierarchies; the topic was peripheral.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from its egalitarian aims and openness to state action to correct inequality.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred: Cohen's critique of self-ownership and Roemer's focus on unequal asset endowments reject first-claim title as a source of rightful ownership.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the school's liberal-egalitarian ethics; the sources do not discuss international criminal law.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: the school is secular and analytic, and nothing in the sources endorses scriptural literalism.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian commitment to equal standing; not discussed in the sources.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: the school largely abandons classical Marxist state-socialist models and favours market socialism, so defending a bureaucratic planned state is split.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: Wright's and Przeworski's work favours democratic institutions with direct popular accountability, not delegate chains.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the school's secular egalitarianism, which gives no group special legal status.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; members are split between cosmopolitan and group-rights positions.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; democratic instincts suggest support but the school has no stated position.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no stated position on decolonisation borders.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: Cohen praises community and equality, but analytical Marxists favour abundance-based egalitarian socialism over asceticism.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian and universalist commitments; not discussed by the sources.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian commitment to equal treatment of women and men in civic duties.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred; analytical Marxists use rational-choice and individualist methods and are not attached to spiritual national bonds.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian, rights-respecting political philosophy of the school; no sources address drug policy.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not addressed; the school's concerns are exploitation, justice and class, not foreign alignment.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from the school's cosmopolitan egalitarianism, which does not favour kin-based state duties.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Cohen, Van Parijs and Roemer's circle treat natural resources as owed equally to all, with compensation or taxation for those who take more.

self-ownership.rationale: Cohen argued against the self-ownership thesis because it blocks egalitarian redistribution, though some members (Roemer, Elster) were less hostile.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Not addressed; adherents favour redistribution but have no recorded view on sales taxes specifically.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred; Van Parijs's universal basic income and the school's egalitarianism favour universal provision over targeting.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred from Wright's real utopias, which favour democratic participation and empowered civic associations rather than bypassing intermediaries.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the school's egalitarian opposition to unearned advantages.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from the school's liberal-egalitarian, secular approach to politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Not addressed; the school's view of technology is as a source of productive capacity for socialism, not a choice involving ancestral values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the school's egalitarian commitment to equal liberty for all.

national-resource-control.rationale: Not addressed; the school is internationalist but is not hostile to public control of resources.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Cohen's Why Not Socialism? and his critique of Nozick judge justice by equality of access to advantage, not by the history of how holdings came about.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from general left support for taxing finance; the sources do not discuss it.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred; the school treats class as primary but grants that racial disadvantage is not eliminated, and does not discuss it directly.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Not addressed; analytical philosophers are split on natural-law claims and the school has no stated position.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from Cohen's and Van Parijs's interest in freedom from toil and in a basic income.

multipolar-world.rationale: Not addressed; the school's concerns are domestic distribution and class, not geopolitical order.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Roemer, Elster and Cohen rejected or discarded the labour theory of value as unsound while keeping a theory of exploitation.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism is peripheral to the school's concerns and adherents are not recorded as taking a position.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred; the school is egalitarian and attentive to both class and equal treatment, but adherents are not recorded as ranking them.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Roemer's A Future for Socialism defends market socialism, but the school favours democratic rather than communist-party rule, so the premise is only partly accepted.

missingStatements.text: Capitalism is unjust mainly because productive assets are very unequally owned, not because workers' labour is stolen.
missingStatements.rationale: Roemer states that capitalism is unjust because of sharply unequal ownership of the means of production, separate from the technical measure of exploitation.
missingStatements.declined: An intra-Marxist dispute about the theory of exploitation; profit-exploitation covers the question other ideologies can answer.

missingStatements.text: Social scientific explanations should be built from the actions and beliefs of individuals rather than from the functions of social wholes.
missingStatements.rationale: Elster defends methodological individualism as the only appropriate form of social explanation, a defining commitment of the school.
missingStatements.declined: A methodological position in social science rather than a political question.

missingStatements.text: A society can combine market exchange with equal or social ownership of productive capital.
missingStatements.rationale: Roemer's market socialism and Wright's real utopias rest on markets with socially or equally owned capital.

notes: Strands differ: Cohen emphasises community and equality ethics, Roemer formal models, Elster rational choice and scepticism of general laws of history, Wright empirical class analysis and real utopias, Van Parijs basic income. Most statements outside political economy have no school position, so their answers are inferred.
